title: When One Agent Becomes Two
subtitle: Monday, the morning your midterm is in: one agent handles a bike shop's inbox, then a researcher → writer → critic pipeline handles the same email, and you read the handoff and the bill. Wednesday: the one-agent test on your own agent, an org chart, and a critic in ten lines.
heroTitle: When One Agent Becomes Two

objectives.title: Split for a Reason · Hand Off with a Contract · Check Before You Send
objectives.description: The one outcome: you can say in one sentence why an agent should be two (permissions, specialization, isolation, parallelism) or why it should stay one, and you can show the document that passes between them.

objectives.title: Run the Same Email Two Ways
objectives.description: A solo agent reads, drafts and sends; a researcher → writer → critic pipeline does it with a JSON brief, a verdict and a human gate. Bet on the call count, then read the bill on Flash and on Argon.

objectives.title: Break a Team Four Ways
objectives.description: The telephone game at the handoff, a customer email that gives the agent orders, four calls to say you're welcome, and two agents that never agree. Then fix one.

objectives.title: Apply It to Your Own Agent
objectives.description: The one-agent test on your midterm, an org chart with four boxes, and a critic in ten lines that reviews every answer against the tool outputs it came from.

agenda.title: Meeting 1 · Midterm Pulse + The Telephone Game
agenda.description: Three 'what it refused' sentences from your memos. Then you run a pipeline by hand: a reader whispers the returns policy, a writer replies to Maya, a checker with the page stops the first wrong promise.
bulletPoints: One agent did everything. That is usually right — today is about the exceptions, and the only honest rule for them: name the reason
Three ways to split: pipeline, router, critic. Permissions, specialization, isolation, parallelism
The handoff must be a document, not a whisper; the checker must never write what it checks

agenda.title: Live, Then Hands-On: Maya Wants Her Money Back
agenda.description: A helmet, 45 days, seal intact. The solo agent on the projector, then the pipeline — bet on the model calls first. Then on your own key, answering the 🚦 yourself.
bulletPoints: Did the solo agent search before it wrote, and what did it promise?
Read the brief: JSON with sources. The writer saw nothing else
The bill: solo versus pipeline, Flash versus Argon. Then: for which emails?

agenda.title: Part 5 Together: When Does a Team Fail?
agenda.description: A fact lost at the handoff, Derek's P.S. aimed at the agent, Priya's thank-you costing four calls, and a writer and critic that never agree.
bulletPoints: The router is one call; the circuit breaker is one number
Fix the one that bothered you most. Never a fourth agent

agenda.title: Wrap: Boardroom + Wednesday
agenda.description: Why is the vendor's product five agents, what passes between them, who checks and did they write it, what does one email cost.
bulletPoints: Wednesday: bring your midterm notebook — the one-agent test is on yours
HW #8 Catch-Up is open, due Thu Nov 12

agenda.title: Meeting 2 · Midterm Debrief + Monday in One Slide
agenda.description: Three memo sentences, anonymous: what it refused, what it cost, one agent or two. Then the three rules in one slide.
bulletPoints: The memo line most of you lost points on is the one we fix today

agenda.title: Hands-On: The One-Agent Test, On Yours
agenda.description: Write the sentence 'my agent should be two because ___' or leave it one. Paste the critic under your agent and run your five tests through it. Then pairs draw the org chart and trade.
bulletPoints: Find one FAIL and decide whether the critic was right — that row goes in the final memo
Four boxes: reads, decides, acts, checks. Circle the one that reads untrusted text. Does it hold the keys?

agenda.title: The Bill + From Midterm to Final
agenda.description: Solo versus pipeline versus Argon in the Cost of Thinking calculator, the price of one wrong promise, and the road to the final: HW #8, HW #9 pitch, your midterm as the starting point.
bulletPoints: HW #8 Catch-Up due Thu Nov 12 · HW #9 Final Project Pitch due Thu Nov 19
Monday: Session 9, agents for your industry — bring the industry you want to work in

agenda.title: Same Model, Different Harness
agenda.description: One photo, one model, three harnesses. Bet how many of Level 0's objects a 3D pipeline would reject, watch the rules from a real open-source product cut the count, then run it on a photo of your own desk.
bulletPoints: Level 0 just asks · Level 1 adds four rules · Level 2 adds a check in code and one fix — Monday's critic in a new costume
Rules make it likely; code makes it checked. Every rejected line is a paid 3D generation thrown away
For your HW #9 pitch: one rule written down, one check in code, one human gate

agenda.title: Wrap
agenda.description: Close. Midterm questions after class or by email.

activities.title: The Same Email, Two Ways (Mon Nov 2)
activities.description: Parts 1–5 of the notebook, on your own key:

steps.title: Read email 2 to the end
steps.description: Derek's P.S. was not written for a human.

steps.title: The solo agent on Maya
steps.description: Answer the 🚦 yourself. Did it search before it wrote? Refund or store credit? Note the bill.

steps.title: Bet, then the pipeline
steps.description: How many model calls? Run it, read the brief, read the critic's verdict, compare the bills on Flash and Argon.

activities.title: The One-Agent Test, On Yours (Wed Nov 4)

steps.title: Write the sentence
steps.description: 'My agent should be two because ___.' Permissions, specialization, isolation, or parallelism. Can't finish it? It stays one.

steps.title: Add the critic
steps.description: Paste check() under your agent, run your five tests through it, find one FAIL and decide whether the critic was right.

steps.title: Draw the org chart
steps.description: Reads, decides, acts, checks. Trade with a neighbor. Circle the box that reads untrusted text.

activities.discussionNote: Most midterms are right to stay one agent. The critic is the exception worth making every time: one call, nothing to defend.

takeaways.text: Name the reason or don't split. Permissions, specialization, isolation, parallelism. 'It felt complicated' is not on the list.
The handoff is a document. A whisper loses facts; a brief with sources does not. If what passes between agents is 'a prompt,' you have the telephone game.
The critic never writes. One call that checks the answer against the tool outputs. The cheapest second agent, and the one Air Canada needed.
Isolate the part that reads strangers. Emails, pages and documents can give orders. The box that reads them must not hold the keys.
More agents, more bill, not more intelligence. Route the thank-you notes around the pipeline. Price one wrong promise before you decide.
